title: StageRecord
description: One stage as the document stores it.

version.description: The version of the stage's contract: which schema its settings and output follow.

depends_on.description:
The hash of the input the stage read, so staleness can be worked out on load. Absent until
the stage has run.

settings.description: The settings the stage ran with (or will run with).

output.description: What the stage returned. Absent until the stage has run.

centreline.description: The river centreline the levels are read on, from the mouth when one is stated.

design_line.description: The design line the stages after this one read.

given.description: The water profile of the inputs, on river chainage.

pools.description: The pools, in order of river chainage. Empty: no pools.

beyond_pools.description: What the level is outside every pool.

step_m.description: The step between points of the answer, metres of design-line chainage.

Polyline.description: A line in the project CRS: `[x, y]` points in order.

WaterProfile.description:
The water level along a river: points sorted by chainage, read linearly between points and held
flat beyond the first and last. Two points at one chainage make a step (a weir): at that chainage
the later point holds.

WaterPoint.description:
One point of a water level profile: a river chainage and the level there, in metres. It is
written as the pair `[chainage, level]`.

Pool.description: One pool: a stretch of river held at one level by the structure at its downstream end.

from.description: River chainage where the pool starts (its downstream end).

to.description: River chainage where the pool ends (its upstream end). Not below `from`.

level_m.description: The pool's design level, metres above datum.

min_level_m.description: The lowest level the pool is held at: navigation depth is checked here (issue 532).

max_level_m.description: The highest level the pool reaches: flood risk is checked here (issue 532).

Chainage.description:
Distance along a river or a design line, in metres. Chainage 0 is at the river mouth when the river
states one (spec 0017); with no mouth stated, it is at the start of the line as it was given.

BeyondPools.description: What the level is outside every pool.

oneOf.description:
The pools' levels, read as one stepped profile and held flat beyond its ends. How the
optimise stage's pools have always been read; the default, so no stored number moves.
The river's own level, from the given profile (open river below the lowest weir).

DesignWater.description: What the water stage returns: the water level along the design line.

points.description: The points, in order of design-line chainage; two at a step.

stretches.description: The stretches, in order, with no gap between them.

river_chainage.description: The river chainage the point projects to, where its level was read.

level_m.description: The design water level, metres above datum.

min_level_m.description: The pool's minimum level, inside a pool that has one.

max_level_m.description: The pool's maximum level, inside a pool that has one.

held_flat.description: True beyond the ends of the profile that sets the level: the nearer end's level, held flat.

oneOf.description: The water profile of the inputs.
A pool held by a structure.
The river's own level, outside every pool.

Between two pools that do not touch: read straight from the lower pool's level to the upper
one's (how the optimise stage's pools have always been read).

WaterStretch.description: A stretch of design line whose level comes from one source (and one pool).

pool.description: The pool it lies in: its index in the input's pools.

held_flat.description: True beyond the ends of the profile that sets the level.
